q: The Borel-Cantelli lemma (first): if Σ μ(Eₙ) < ∞, then μ(lim sup Eₙ) = 0 (almost every point is in at most finitely many Eₙ). The second Borel-Cantelli lemma requires independence and states:
opts: Σ μ(Eₙ) = ∞ implies μ(lim sup Eₙ) = 0
If the Eₙ are independent and Σ μ(Eₙ) = ∞, then μ(lim sup Eₙ) = 1 (a.e. point is in infinitely many Eₙ)
If Eₙ are disjoint, μ(lim sup Eₙ) = 1
exp: Second Borel-Cantelli: independence + Σ μ(Eₙ) = ∞ → μ(lim sup Eₙ) = 1. This is the 'converse' under independence. Without independence, the conclusion fails (e.g., Eₙ = E for all n and μ(E) = 1 gives Σ μ(Eₙ) = ∞ but lim sup Eₙ = E — fine, but correlated).
